title: Android TextView: multiline width
purpose: Check that a wrap-content TextView measures its longest line when its XML text uses a Unicode next-line separator.
changes: Wrap-content measurement now recognizes all of the mandatory line separators already handled by the wrapping code. The example compares a two-line view with a single-line view containing the same longest line.
steps: At the top, compare the green two-line box containing WWW and i with the peach box containing WWW.
The boxes should have the same width because WWW is the longest line in both. The i should appear on a second line in the green box.
Choose OK if it looks correct, or Reject with details and your device.
expected: Both boxes have the same width, and the first box displays two lines.
limits: The example uses the Unicode next-line separator. Android device handling of these separators, font metrics and complete text shaping remain unverified.

references.scope: Unicode line-break opportunities used by Bhoo.

validation: 197 Android XML tests and 156 importer tests passed. A Rust test checks width and rendered lines for CRLF and all supported Unicode mandatory separators.
A 320 × 650 browser test checked both rendered lines and equal background widths.
